Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Pinnacle Financial Services Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Pinnacle Financial Services Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are David Larson, Chief Executive Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; and Karen Novak, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to David Larson.

David Larson:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Pinnacle Financial Services Inc. delivered solid performance in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Enhancing customer experience
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Investing in strategic growth initiatives
4. Maintaining strong capital levels.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our key strategic initiatives and the progress we've made. These efforts are built around our three-pillar framework: accelerating digital transformation, deepening customer relationships through embedded finance and wealth solutions, and fortifying sustainable growth with prudent risk management. This approach is tailored to create long-term shareholder value amid ongoing challenges like persistent inflation, the Fed funds rate stabilizing at 5.25-5.50% after hikes, and shifting regulations such as Basel IV in Europe and U.S. Dodd-Frank stress tests.

Starting with digital transformation, our top priority, we've committed $450 million in capital expenditures this year, up 25% from last year. This investment targets AI-driven personalization, cloud-native systems, and open banking APIs. We've wrapped up Phase 2 of our core banking upgrade, shifting 85% of retail and commercial loans to our proprietary Pinnacle Cloud Platform on AWS with Kubernetes for flexible microservices. This cut our new feature rollout time from 12 months to 90 days.

The results speak for themselves: digital channels now handle 78% of transactions, up from 62% a year ago, with mobile app logins jumping 32% to 15 million monthly active users. Our AI fraud detection, trained on 2.5 billion past transactions, cut false positives by 40% and blocked $185 million in losses this quarter—beating benchmarks from competitors like JPMorgan Chase, where gains are typically 25-30%. In North America, 55% of our revenue base, digital deposits grew 18% year-over-year to $145 billion, powered by Pinnacle Pay wallets linked to Apple Pay and Google Pay. Over in APAC, our Grab partnership in Singapore and Indonesia added 1.2 million digital customers, lifting remittance fees 45%.

On deepening customer relationships, we're evolving beyond basic banking into full ecosystems with embedded finance and advanced wealth tools. Our Pinnacle Flex Buy Now, Pay Later service originated $2.8 billion this quarter, up 55% year-over-year, holding delinquency at 1.2% via our unique credit scoring that pulls in telematics and social spending data. This delivers bank-level underwriting like Affirm or Klarna but with a 420 basis points net interest margin.

In wealth management, Pinnacle Wealth Hub, using robo-advisory from BlackRock's Aladdin, saw assets under management rise 22% to $320 billion, with net promoter scores up 17 points to 72. New ESG portfolios matching EU SFDR Article 8/9 drew $15 billion from European high-net-worth clients in the green shift. Wealth and asset fees climbed 28% to $1.2 billion, now 22% of non-interest revenue, helping offset NII headwinds.

By region, Europe at 25% of revenue navigated ECB rate differences and PSD3 rules through $180 billion loan growth, up 14%, with commercial real estate capped at 8% post-stress tests via 150+ API integrations for fintechs like Revolut. In Latin America, our Nubank JV in Brazil hit 5 million users and 12% digital SME lending share at Brazil's 10.5% Selic rate, posting 24% ROE.

Our sustainable growth pillar keeps our balance sheet rock-solid, with CET1 at 13.2%, exceeding our 11.5% target and regulatory floors, backed by $12 billion organic tangible common equity YTD. Liquidity coverage ratio is 145%, net stable funding ratio 128%, with deposit beta steady at 35% after tweaking non-operational deposit rates.

On ESG, $3.5 billion in green bonds under our Sustainalytics-verified framework funded solar and EV loans at 4.8% yield. We're on pace for 2030 net-zero lending, with 28% of new loans Paris-aligned versus 15% last year, full TCFD/ISSB Scope 3 reporting, earning an MSCI AA upgrade and $8 billion in sustainable deposits.

We're tackling headwinds like U.S. unemployment at 4.1% and 20% CRE office vacancies by limiting office loans to 4%, adding $250 million provisions for workouts—coverage now 180 bps. Positively, our $1.2 billion Midwest Digital Bank buyout added 800,000 customers and $25 billion low-cost deposits at 2.1%, boosting EPS 8% in year one.

Forward, Q4 brings generative AI chatbots for round-the-clock service, eyeing 20% call center savings from 2.5% of opex, plus embedded insurance with Lemonade and Chubb. Cost-to-income fell to 54.2%, down 210 bps year-over-year, heading to 52% via RPA on 65% of back-office work.

Overall, these moves fueled 12% revenue growth, 15% EPS gains, and 16.8% ROTCE—top-quartile among KBW large-cap peers. We're not just weathering the storm; we're leading through it.

I will now turn the call over to Robert Hayes to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Robert Hayes:
Thank you, David, and good morning. Pinnacle Financial Services Inc. reported net income of $850 million for the Q3, or $2.15 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% year-over-year driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Non-interest income was impacted by softer trading revenues amid rate volatility. We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 13.2%. 

Let me expand on a few key areas. First, our provision for credit losses came in at $425 million this quarter, up 18% from the prior quarter and 42% year-over-year, equating to 45 basis points of average loans versus 32 bps last year. This builds our allowance for credit losses to 1.42% of loans held for investment, up from 1.28% last quarter, consistent with peers like JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America given macro uncertainties.

The provision stems from portfolio performance, macro overlays, and targeted adjustments. Portfolio credit drove about 55% of it: consumer delinquencies edged to 1.85% on $45 billion credit cards from 1.62% last quarter, hit by inflation and rate lags; auto loans at $32 billion held 30-day delinquencies at 2.1% but charge-offs annualized to 1.85% with better repossession values; mortgages steady at 0.9% NPLs on equity buffers. Commercial and industrial plus CRE accounted for 65% of the provision uptick—CRE office at $18 billion saw criticized assets to 12% from 9% amid 20% U.S. gateway vacancies like New York and San Francisco, mirroring Wells Fargo trends; multifamily $25 billion hit Stage 2 at 8% from Sun Belt rent issues. Net charge-offs totaled $320 million or 0.85% annualized, above last year's 0.72% but under our 1.05% decade average.

Macro overlays added 30%, via CECL's scenario weighting—65% base, 25% adverse, 10% severe—with GDP cut to 1.2% for 2024, unemployment to 4.6%, CRE cap rates to 7.5%, lifting PDs 15-20 bps. U.S. (75% loans) showed consumer strength at 3.8% unemployment but CRE weakness; Europe (15%) up 25% on German C&I slowdowns; APAC (10%) flat on China stimulus despite property.

Adjustments were 15%: $65 million for Permian energy at sub-$80 oil; sold $2.5 billion non-core CRE at premium.

Our CECL/IFRS 9 ECL uses discounted cash flows by risk pools—FICO for consumers, NaICS for C&I. PD via logistic regression on 200+ variables plus ML gradient boosting since Q4 2023, up 12% accuracy like Capital One; LGD downturn at 45% CRE, 65% cards with yield haircuts; EAD behavioral for revolvers. Q-factors: +15 bps CRE policy, -5 bps consumer strength. ACL roll: $3.2 billion start, +$425 million provision, -$320 million NCOs, +$50 million originations, to $3.355 billion.

Tech-wise, GenAI scenarios since May cut run-times 40%; Deloitte validation clean; blockchain collateral pilot.

We're proactive: CET1 11.8% post-returns enables 4-6% 2024 loan growth in C&I ($120 billion), digital deposits; CRE LTV to 65%, unsecured pricing +25 bps. Q4 PCL $400-475 million or 38-48 bps on stable macros; recession risk 35%, CRE watch like New York Community Bancorp.

Next, net interest income hit $2.48 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, topping expectations with NIM at 3.52%, +15 bps from Q2—the third straight expansion. Asset yields to 5.85% (+8 bps) on securities at 4.75% and C&I re-pricing to 6.45% (45% loans) at SOFR+250 bps. Funding at 2.33% via 35% beta below peers' 45-50%; DDA up 4% to $185 billion (28% deposits); total deposits $425 billion, L/D 82%.

U.S. Southeast/Midwest loan growth 2.1% led by C&I and CRE conversions in Nashville/Charlotte; Northeast softer equipment offset by mortgage warehouses; Europe $150 million NII on 4.2% Euribor, 60% hedged.

We optimized $5 billion securities—sold 2.8% MBS for SOFR floaters, +$1.2 billion sensitivity, 65% asset-sensitive. Pinnacle Origin8 did $3.2 billion SMB loans at +25 bps margins, AI approvals in 48 hours.

For Q4, NII $2.55-2.60 billion, +3-5%, NIM 3.50-3.55% assuming Fed hold then December 25 bps cut (85% CME odds). Loans +1.5-2% on C&I/renewables; deposits +1%, beta caps costs. Adjusted EPS $1.85-1.95 (+8-12%); fees $850 million (+6%) on $320 billion AUM (+15% wealth), +10% cards; expenses $1.75 billion, efficiency 52% via $100 million GenAI savings like BofA Erica. Provisions $450-500 million, NCOs 28 bps, NPLs 65 bps, reserves 1.15%; ROTCE 16.5-17%, CET1 11.2% post-$1.2 billion buyback of $5 billion program.

Into 2025, NIM rebound potential; $120 billion cash, LCR 145% guards vs outflows like New York Community. Focus: growth, 35% fee revenue, capital returns.

Finally, on risk-weighted assets management, total RWAs at $528 billion, +1.8% quarter-over-quarter from $519 billion, +6.2% year-over-year. Credit RWAs $381 billion (72%) +2.1%; market $58 billion +1.5% on fixed income; ops $89 billion flat.

Credit optimizations: CRE RWAs -3% to $92 billion (24%) via paydowns/syndications post-$4.5 billion Q1 sale (-150 bps intensity); consumer $145 billion +2.5% at 42% weights (LTV 65%); CIB $144 billion +3.2% at 78% IRB.

IRB covers 88% credit (+6% YoY), 8-10% relief vs standardized like JPM/HSBC; $25 million model ML for PD/LGD/IFRS 9 ECL, e.g., SME -2.2 billion RWAs on UK landing.

Regions: North America $222 billion (42%) +2.4% on IG corporates/CCAR 13.2%; Europe $185 billion (35%) flat de-risking shipping -15%; APAC $95 billion (18%) +4.1% infra at 55% weights, hedged; EM 5% 120% floor.

RWA intensity 48.2% from 49.1% YoY on quality shift. Initiatives: $8 billion auto ABS offloads $6.5 billion RWAs; $15 billion CVA hedges -12%; AI warnings on $300 billion wholesale; Basel IV 72.5% floor stress +15% modeled absorbed.

FY RWA +5-7%, Q4 softer; backs $0.85-0.90 EPS, 11%+ ROE, 12.8% CET1 buffer.

We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star then 1. Our first question comes from Mike Sullivan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Sullivan:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on progress with your key strategic initiatives, particularly digital transformation?

David Larson:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, as I outlined earlier, our digital push is gaining real momentum—78% transaction shift to digital channels, 15 million monthly app users, and that AI fraud engine saving $185 million this quarter alone. The cloud migration and API expansions are accelerating everything from customer onboarding in APAC to embedded finance here at home. It's core to our priorities and already diversifying revenue streams effectively.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Wong:
Good morning. What is your outlook for NII and earnings guidance into next quarter?

Robert Hayes:
Good morning, Jennifer. As detailed, Q4 NII guides to $2.55-2.60 billion with NIM steady at 3.50-3.55%, assuming that Fed pause and late cut. EPS $1.85-1.95, supported by fee growth and efficiency gains. Our asset sensitivity and deposit franchise give us good tailwinds even if rates ease gradually.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the CRE market on your loan portfolio?

Karen Novak:
Good morning, Alex. We've been deliberate here—CRE office exposure tightly managed at $18 billion with criticized up to 12% on those 20% vacancies, but overall CRE at 8% of loans post-stress, coverage 180 bps. Provisions reflected the prudence at $425 million, with de-risking like the $2.5 billion sale, and underwriting tightened to 65% LTV. Credit metrics remain solid below historical averages.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to David Larson for any closing remarks.

David Larson:
Thank you for your interest in Pinnacle Financial Services Inc. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
